text:
anya: Heads up — vendor pushed a new FlashAttention variant upstream (flashattn v2.4.1). Early local runs show a perf regression for paged-KV workloads. Can eng-runtime take a look? cc @mike @david

mike: Saw the PR. Any quick repro steps? :eyes:

david: Ran a quick perf pass on rbuild20: model=gpt-j, seq=2048, batch=4, kv-mode=paged. Baseline (pinned flash_v1) tokens/s ~ 8.2k, after vendor patch flash_v2 tokens/s ~ 6.7k. ~18% drop. nvprof shows an extra memcpy and increased kernel time.

anya: Noted. Logs point to a fallback path in the fused kernel that kicks in when seq%32 != 0; vendor changed alignment checks in v2.4.1. Also xFormers recently merged a reorder patch — could be interacting.

lucy: Triage proposal: 1) reproduce cleanly in CI perf job 2) bisect vendor commits to find offending change 3) add temporary routing override to prefer pinned kernel for paged workloads 4) contact vendor and vendor-3p channels with perf logs.

mike: Repro command I'm using: `python perf/run.py --model gpt-j --seq 2048 --batch 4 --kv-mode paged --kernel flash_v2 --runs 20`. Add `--trace` to capture nvprof output.

david: Copied relevant profiling snippet:
```
NVPROF: Profiling result summary
Kernel: flash_attn_v2        Time: 150.4 ms    Calls: 40
Memcpy H2D                 Time: 30.2 ms
Kernel: fused_attn_fallback Time: 45.1 ms
L2 cache miss spike around offsets used by paged KV
```

anya: That memcpy increase looks like extra staging of KV pages — maybe a change in the kernel that prevents pinned page reuse. I'll compare the vendor ABI for their allocator.

mike: Started a bisect on vendor repo. First suspicious commit is 7f3c2a9 which changes the alignment/stride code. Will run perf against that commit next.

david: Quick workaround: disabling async prefetch in our paged loader recovers ~10% (so not full), but it increases CPU usage and latency jitter. Not a long-term fix.

anya: We should prepare a routing config override to route paged-KV requests to `flash_v1_pinned` while we wait for upstream fix. Example config snippet: `kernel_preference: ["flash_v1_pinned", "paged_fallback"]` — canary that on rg-paged-1.

lucy: Action items: Mike = bisect + vendor PR link, David = test routing override + perf regression test, Anya = open vendor issue and collect artifacts, Lucy = notify SRE if we need an emergency rollback plan. Target: EOD.

mike: Bisect update: commits up to 7f3c2a9 are clean; perf drop appears immediately after 7f3c2a9 -> a1b9d4e. Reproduced locally. Filing details.

anya: Also noticed vLLM changed KV packing in a recent commit on their side; pinging research to confirm compatibility. If vLLM and vendor changes both touched stride semantics we might have a multi-repo interaction.

sre-bot: Incident watcher set for deployment group `rg-paged-1`. No customer-facing incidents detected currently. Alert threshold set to 10% regression.

vendor-bot: Created vendor/flashattn#482 (by anya) linking perf logs and nvprof output, request: bisect-confirmation + repro script.

david: Note: switching to xFormers kernel (where available) doesn't reproduce regression — suggests vendor change is the root cause. Will try a diff of allocator calls.

anya: OK. I'll ping vendor eng and upload the CI perf traces. If vendor provides a patch, we can validate in a canary before updating runtime. Until then, prepare the rollout override.

lucy: Thanks team. Keep updates in this thread. If perf gets worse, escalate to SEV. :thumbsup:

mike: Will post bisect PR link when ready.

anya: pinging @research and @platform-ops for visibility.

(threads ends)
